newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish paper says Astra's Losec may damage skin.
newsitem.headline: Swedish paper says Astra's Losec may damage skin.

text.p: Astra AB's best-selling ulcer treatment drug Losec is suspected of causing serious skin damage, the Swedish tabloid daily Expressen reported.
The newspaper said that four cases of serious skin changes had been reported to the pharmaceutical control board and in one case, a 72-year-old woman had to undergo intensive treatment for one month.
But the newspaper also quoted Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby as rejecting the theory that Losec might have caused the illness.

"We definitely do not associate this with Losec," Ternby said. "Among the millions of people who take Losec there must be all sorts, including some who would have been affected by this in any case," Ternby said.
Ternby was not immediately available for comment on the Expressen report.

The newspaper quoted Orjan Mortimer, a doctor at the pharmaceutical control board, as saying,"In the first three cases of serious skin reaction, the patients had been treated with Losec and other drugs. But in the 72-year-old woman's case, Losec was the only drug in question."
The four cases were all diagnosed as Lyells syndrome, a serious skin complaint.
Expressen said the pharmaceutical board had instructed all doctors to report all serious cases of skin reaction in patients treated with Losec or other drugs.
Astra's share price dipped 2.5 crowns to 309 on the newspaper report.

"This has had an effect on the share price although it shouldn't really because everyone knows that Astra has an extensive database on the effects of Losec," said one broker, who added he felt the dip would be short-lived.
